en.title: Good Subsequence with Limited Adjacent Changes
en.description:
Choose the longest subsequence in which the number of adjacent pairs with unequal values is at most k. Elements of the original array may be skipped.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n values. Original constraints: 1≤n≤500, 1≤value≤10⁹, 0≤k≤min(n,25).
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 5; 3; 1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Maintain dp[value][j], the longest length ending with value using at most j changes, and the global best best[j] for each j. Update j in decreasing order, taking the better of extending the same value and best[j−1]+1.
